_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the AI Website Creator roadmap rendered at /ai-dev-kit/ai-website-creator. The AI Website Creator is NOT an extension — it lives in the AI Dev Kit (skills + docs/recipes + the generalized vertical-template library) and drives the plugin's existing fresh-build and Site Converter paths. Task `status` is maintained by `npm run roadmap:site-creator` (scripts/gen-roadmap.mjs), which resolves the source tree via `cloneDir` (the AI Dev Kit push clone) and flips a task to `done` when everything in its `detect` block exists there. Nothing is built yet, so every unpinned task is `planned` — correct before any code exists. Hand-edit title/detail/detect freely; set `pin: true` on a concept task with no single file footprint.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · The archetype catalogue
milestones.goal: A curated set of **section archetypes**, each a small recipe that emits **page-builder JSON + Unyson+ shortcodes + Animation Engine effects**, with colour and type coming from **Theme Settings presets** rather than baked onto each element. Start where the demand is — heroes, navbars, feature grids, CTAs, footers, marquees — not at a hundred thin entries.

tasks.title: Recipe format
tasks.detail: One document shape every recipe follows: *when to use it*, *the composition* (the exact shortcode arrangement as a builder-JSON template), *the motion* (which Animation Engine effect pairs with it, and the restrained default), *the tokens* (which Theme Settings presets it expects), and *a live preview* (a link to our own demo page). The format is the contract the composition guide and the create-site skill both read.

tasks.title: Hero recipes
tasks.detail: The highest-frequency archetype by a wide margin. A handful of genuinely good heroes (centered, split, editorial-oversized, media-backed), each as a builder-JSON template with restrained motion and preset-driven type.

tasks.title: Navbar recipes
tasks.detail: Universal header patterns built on the Header/Footer Builder: logo, primary nav from the sitemap, an accessible mobile menu, an active-page state, and the primary CTA.

tasks.title: Feature-grid recipes
tasks.detail: Icon-box and card grids for features, services and benefits, mapped to the real shortcodes with preset-owned card skins (never per-element copies).

tasks.title: CTA recipes
tasks.detail: Conversion blocks — banner CTAs, split CTAs, inverted full-bleed CTAs — with the button skin living on its colour preset.

tasks.title: Footer recipes
tasks.detail: Universal footer patterns on the Footer Builder: brand summary, navigation, the primary conversion path, and legal links once they exist.

tasks.title: Marquee & logo-strip recipes
tasks.detail: Moving strips for logos, words and proof, using the native marquee element with reduced-motion handling built in.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · The style library
milestones.goal: A curated set of named **design directions** a person can pick from — the "make the design <style>" input. A style is not a theme file; it is a mapping from a look to **Theme Settings presets** (palette, fonts, radius, borders, spacing), the **Animation Engine** register that fits it (instant vs. cinematic), and the section treatments that express its personality. We take the *taxonomy and the design thinking* from the public design-prompt libraries; every style is re-authored here in our own vocabulary, because those prompts describe React and Tailwind components, not page-builder output.

tasks.title: Style model
tasks.detail: How a named style resolves to a design system: the Theme Settings preset set it writes, the type pairing, the radius/border/texture rules, and the Animation Engine defaults. One model so every style is described the same way and the picker can list them.

tasks.title: Map to the existing aesthetic skills
tasks.detail: Several directions already exist as design skills — a refined default, minimalist, brutalist, and a high-end "expensive-agency" look. A style entry points at the matching skill where one exists, and only carries a new recipe where there is a genuine gap, so the library reuses rather than duplicates.

tasks.title: Seed the high-value styles
tasks.detail: A first set drawn from the demand we can see: a monochrome editorial look (pure black and white, serif hero, zero radius, line textures, inversion hover), a newsprint look, a Swiss/Bauhaus grid look, a modern dark look, a terminal look, a luxury look, and a kinetic/motion-led look. Each is a design direction expressed as Theme Settings presets plus section treatments — authored here, never copied.

tasks.title: The style picker
tasks.detail: The intake step that offers the styles as an enumerated choice (the "dropdown"), with a *describe-your-own* escape hatch so the curated set is never a cage. In the kit this is a choice in the create-site flow; in a later in-admin or hosted surface it becomes a visual picker with thumbnails — same list, no rework. **Landed with Phase 4.** It is the style step of the create-site intake: skills/create-site/inputs/brief.md offers the seven styles as an enumerated choice with a describe-your-own option, and the spec carries the result as brand.style plus brand.style_notes — the escape hatch that keeps the curated set from being a cage. A visual picker with thumbnails is the same list in a later surface, not a rework.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · The composition guide
milestones.goal: A catalogue of parts is not a site. This is the sequencing layer that turns a chosen style and a set of archetypes into a coherent page, and it slots onto the existing build protocol rather than replacing it: **design system first → chrome (header/footer) → sections, region by region → motion → ship gate.** The generator is no more allowed to skip to "write sections" than a careful human build is.

tasks.title: Composition guide
tasks.detail: The ordering rules, the page-shape heuristics (which archetypes a given page type wants, and in what sequence), and the hand-off into the build protocol's phases and gates.

tasks.title: Ship-gate wiring
tasks.detail: Every composed page carries the same accessibility, SEO and performance obligations as everything else we ship — reduced-motion handling, a sane Web Vitals cost, real content in the HTML — checked with the kit's `tools/measure` harness. A page that fails the gate does not ship.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · The create-site skill
milestones.goal: The single entry point the person runs in their own Claude Code / Cursor through the AI Dev Kit. One flow, four ways in: a plain-language **brief**, a **reference URL**, a **design reference** (screenshot / image), or a **vertical template**. It gathers a structured spec, then drives the build protocol (or the Site Converter for the URL and design-reference paths) to a finished, editable Unyson+ site.

tasks.title: Skill scaffold
tasks.detail: A `create-site` skill under the kit's reserved `skills/` folder: a `SKILL.md` that wires the intake, the style picker, the archetype catalogue, the composition guide and the ship gate into one routed flow.

tasks.title: Site spec
tasks.detail: A structured description of the site — business, pages, brand, style, sections, SEO, compliance — generalized from the CRM website generator's `site-spec.json`. The spec, not a prose prompt, is the source of truth the build reads.

tasks.title: Input: a brief
tasks.detail: From a plain-language brief ("a barber shop, warm and dark, booking-led") to the spec: propose a sitemap, pick a style and archetypes, fill copy, choose a palette. The fresh-build path — the only input that skips capture.

tasks.title: Input: a reference URL
tasks.detail: Hand the URL to the capture service and Site Converter, which produce a native build; the creator then refines it through the same composition and ship-gate steps. Reuses the converter end to end rather than re-implementing it.

tasks.title: Input: a design reference
tasks.detail: From an uploaded screenshot or image: read the look (palette, type, spacing, treatment) into a style and tokens, without copying the reference's content, logos or distinctive layout. Captures the design, builds original content on it.

tasks.title: Input: a vertical template
tasks.detail: Pick an industry starting point and let the creator customize it — the CRM-generator pattern, generalized (see Phase 6).

tasks.title: Build rules ported from the field
tasks.detail: The durable rules a good WordPress build follows, as the creator's own: editable builder output (never static HTML or one big Custom HTML block), one universal header and footer, drafts not published until asked, native Unyson+ / theme SEO configured against the real business details, and no invented testimonials, metrics, pricing or claims.

milestones.title: Phase 5 · Content maintenance
milestones.goal: After the site exists, keep it growing. A separate flow for creating a page or post around a topic: research and recommend, wait for approval, draft and optimize for SEO, then publish only on an explicit second approval. Two gates, never one.

tasks.title: Content skill
tasks.detail: A `content` flow in the kit that uses the existing site and its records as the source of truth, so it never re-asks for business, audience or brand facts already known.

tasks.title: Research & recommend (gate 1)
tasks.detail: Study the sitemap, internal links, the topic and search intent; return page-vs-post, angles, titles, a heading structure, the internal links to add, and the specific expert questions only the owner can answer. Wait for approval before drafting. **Landed in skills/create-site/content.md, step 1.** Returns page-vs-post with the reason, the angle (including "improve the page you already have" when that is the honest answer), title options, the heading structure, the internal links in both directions, and the expert questions only the owner can answer — then waits. A draft written before those answers is generic content with their name on it.

tasks.title: Draft & optimize
tasks.detail: Create an editable draft in the current design system, set title, permalink, meta and schema, run the native SEO checks, add genuinely-relevant internal links, and never keyword-stuff or invent facts to satisfy a score. **Landed in skills/create-site/content.md, step 2.** Editable builder content in the existing design system, with the native seo extension fields set as discrete meta keys (_fw_seo_title / _fw_seo_description / _fw_seo_canonical / the og and twitter pairs), where an empty value deletes the row and a cleared template falls through to auto. Explicitly forbids keyword-stuffing and inventing facts to satisfy a score — if the piece needs a fact nobody has, go back and ask.

tasks.title: Publish (gate 2)
tasks.detail: Publish the approved draft only on an explicit go-ahead — do not rewrite it — then verify the public URL, canonical and SEO metadata. **Landed in skills/create-site/content.md, step 3.** Publishes only the draft that was read — no tidying between approval and publishing, because then what goes live is not what was approved — and verifies the live URL, permalink, rendered title and description, canonical, both link directions, and that no staging noindex survived.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · Vertical templates
milestones.goal: Generalize the CRM website generator into the creator's vertical-template layer, so an industry is a starting point rather than a separate product. The CRM Generator becomes the first vertical; its industry presets become the model for the shared library.

tasks.title: Vertical-template format
tasks.detail: The generalized, non-industry form of the CRM generator's industry presets: pages, copy, forms, the spec and the build wording for a vertical, as data the create-site flow reads.

tasks.title: CRM as the first vertical
tasks.detail: Fold the CRM website generator in as the first vertical-template provider: its spec and prompts already drive the AI Dev Kit fresh-build path, so it is the proof the pattern works. The CRM pipeline, forms and newsletter CRM come switched on for this vertical. **Folded in by routing and documentation, not by code.** The generator stays the emitter: its nine presets are listed as the available set in docs/site-creator/verticals/catalogue.md, the create-site vertical input routes CRM-shaped sites to it, and the spec schema carries its lead_capture and crm blocks as optional vertical extensions so what it emits is read directly. There is no code integration and none is needed for it to be the first provider.

tasks.title: Further verticals
tasks.detail: A handful more, drawn from the generator's existing set (local business, professional service, ecommerce, SaaS), each a vertical template the creator can start from and customize.

milestones.title: Phase 6b · The design standard
milestones.goal: The pipeline could measure whether a created site was **fast, reachable and indexed**, and nothing in it could say whether the site was any **good** — so a generator left alone produced competent, forgettable pages forever. This phase adds the second measurement: a four-part design rubric (Design 40 / Usability 30 / Creativity 20 / Content 10), a **theatre level** chosen from what the site is for rather than from enthusiasm, and **one signature moment** per site built from the framework's own machinery.

tasks.title: The rubric and its floor
tasks.detail: The four weighted criteria restated for a page-builder site, scored 0–10 each with one line of evidence per score, floor **7.0 weighted and nothing below 6**. Includes the honesty rules that stop a self-scored pass from flattering itself: score the whole site rather than the home hero, attach a named defect to every point lost, and run the scoring as its own step rather than as a sentence appended by whoever just built it.

tasks.title: Theatre levels — Full, Measured, Quiet
tasks.detail: The bar never moves; the spectacle does. **Measured is the default**, because reading "award-grade" as "every module at once" puts a cinematic hero on a loan application and scores *worse* — usability is 30% on its own, and a finance page drowning in motion reads as a site that is not serious about money. An explicit "simple", "basic" or "minimal" routes to Quiet; a brand launch or an explicit "premium" routes to Full. The level is named in one line with its reason before building, the way the build protocol makes you name a stack.

tasks.title: One signature moment per site
tasks.detail: Exactly one idea a visitor would describe out loud — per site, not per page — with everything around it deliberately quiet. Qualifies only when it belongs to this business (moved to a competitor, it breaks), sits on the path the visitor already takes, survives reduced motion / keyboard / a slow phone with the fallback specified alongside it, and is built from an Animation Engine module, a Kinetic Scene, the Motion Gallery or a page transition rather than a bespoke script the person could never edit. The strongest moments are **participatory** — something the visitor operates, made of the subject itself.

tasks.title: The scored pass in the ship gate
tasks.detail: Check 5 of the created-site ship gate, so the design score is a gate rather than a report: a page that measures clean but scores below the floor is not finished, for the same reason a slow one is not. It gives the gate's one unautomatable instruction — *open the page and look at it* — a pass mark.

symbols.pattern: It is scored, not just measured

tasks.title: Per-style signature vocabularies
tasks.detail: Every style file names the two-to-four moves its direction actually wants, the one it must **never** use, and its reduced-motion answer — so a cinematic reveal never lands on a Swiss grid, a luxury site never bounces, and a newsprint page never animates through a third dimension it does not have. Adds a sixth required section to the style contract.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · The style gallery
milestones.goal: A rendered Unyson+ example per style, so a person can see before they pick — and so the gallery doubles as proof of what the creator makes. Built on our own demos network, listed on the demos home, never a copy of anyone else's preview media.

tasks.title: A demo page per style
tasks.detail: One native Unyson+ page per seeded style, each the same content rendered through that style's presets, so the differences are the design and nothing else. **Specified, not built.** docs/site-creator/gallery.md is the spec, and writing it surfaced a correction: a style is site-wide Theme Settings, so seven styles cannot coexist on one site. The gallery is seven demo SITES (one subsite each on the demos network) running identical content, not seven pages — the obvious reading would have produced seven pages fighting one design system, discovered only after all seven existed. Pinned because the demos live outside the kit tree, where no file can prove them.

tasks.title: Listed on the demos home
tasks.detail: Each style demo gets a card on the demos home grid, so it is discoverable and never orphaned, per the house rule for demos.

milestones.title: Phase 8 · Product surface
milestones.goal: Make it easy for a non-expert to drive. v1 is the kit itself — install the AI Dev Kit, point your agent at your WordPress, run the create-site flow — with onboarding that explains exactly that. An in-admin wizard and a hosted web app are later surfaces on the same proven engine, not v1.

tasks.title: Onboarding
tasks.detail: The guided "how to use it" path: install the kit, connect the agent to the target WordPress, and run the create-site flow — written so someone who has never used Claude Code can follow it.

tasks.title: In-admin wizard (future)
tasks.detail: The AI Assistant extension drives the whole flow inside wp-admin, so no CLI is needed. A later surface on the same engine.

tasks.title: Hosted app (future)
tasks.detail: A hosted web app that builds and deploys into the person's WordPress. Half of this now exists: the Site Creator is hosted, and it produces the spec. What is still missing is the half that BUILDS — today that needs an agent with file access on the person's own machine. So this item is no longer "a hosted front end"; it is hosted execution, and it is the biggest surface and the most infrastructure. Only once the engine is proven.

tasks.title: One questionnaire, one spec
tasks.detail: The Site Creator (create.unysonplus.com) is the ONLY thing that asks a person what their site should be. It runs in the browser, needs no AI, and emits a site-spec.json against skills/create-site/site-spec.schema.json with per-industry presets. The kit dashboard's Create site tab stopped carrying its own form and became a launcher + receiver: it opens the Site Creator, reads back the prompt or the spec, summarises it (business, pages, action, style, target, missing[]) and hands it to the Kit Assistant or to the person's own agent. Two emitters of one schema had already drifted — the "one action" question reached the spec as `primary_action` on one side, as prompt prose only on the other, and was undeclared in the schema, which is now fixed.

tasks.title: Send a spec straight to the kit
tasks.detail: A "Send to AI Dev Kit" button on the Site Creator that posts the spec to the running kit on localhost, so the person never copies and pastes. The dashboard already proxies this pattern for WordPress admin pages, so the mechanism exists. **Blocked on a deliberate decision, not on code:** the chat endpoints currently refuse any origin that is not the dashboard, and that gate is what stops another page in the same browser driving the tools or confirming a proposal. Allowing create.unysonplus.com through must be a narrow allowlist entry made on purpose. Until then, paste covers the same ground.

milestones.title: Phase 9 — Proven on a real build
milestones.goal: Everything above is machinery. None of it is evidence. The creator's own status card on the kit dashboard says "Skill ready · not yet run end to end", and that is the honest state: the archetypes, styles, composition guide, skill and ship gate have never been run together against one real brief, from an empty WordPress to a site someone would show a client. Until that happens, every other improvement is a guess about which part is weakest.

tasks.title: One real site, start to finish
tasks.detail: Take one brief through the whole flow with nothing skipped: Site Creator → spec → agent → a fresh WordPress → the ship gate. Record what broke, which recipe or style was wrong, and what the agent had to be told that the docs should have said. The output that matters is the list of corrections, not the site. The dashboard card may only turn green when this has actually been done.

tasks.title: The status card tells the truth
tasks.detail: Once the flow has been run end to end, the Home card stops saying "not yet run end to end". It says what is true at the time — and if the run exposed gaps, it says that instead of rounding up to Ready.

milestones.title: Phase 10 — Build without an agent
milestones.goal: Today a person needs an AI agent with file access to turn a spec into a site. The spec itself needs no AI at all — the Site Creator writes it in the browser — so the gap is only the build step. A deterministic builder would close it, and would also give the AI path something to be measured against.

tasks.title: Assemble a site from a spec, with no model
tasks.detail: Read a site-spec.json and compose the pages from the kit's own recipes, styles and presets directly — no model in the loop. The spec already names the pages, their shapes, the style and the one action; the recipes already say what each section archetype is. The result would be plainer than an agent's, and it would be exact, free, offline and the same every time. `missing[]` governs it exactly as it governs the agent: a section with no real content is omitted, never invented.

tasks.title: Measured against the agent build
tasks.detail: Run the same spec through both paths and compare them against the ship gate. This is the only way to learn what the model is actually contributing — and if the deterministic build is close, that is the honest default for someone with no AI.
